title: Subjunctive and conditionals
matching: Typed answers ignore letter case, extra spaces, apostrophe style and final . ! or ? punctuation. Accents and every other character count. Multiple-choice answers must match exactly.

lessons.title: Pretérito imperfeito do subjuntivo: forms
lessons.explanation: The imperfect subjunctive is built from the eles form of the pretérito perfeito: remove -ram and add -sse, -sses, -sse, -ssemos, -ssem. Falaram gives falasse; fizeram gives fizesse; tiveram gives tivesse; foram gives fosse; viram gives visse; disseram gives dissesse; vieram gives viesse. The nós form always carries an accent: falássemos, fizéssemos, tivéssemos, fôssemos. Use it after a past main verb that expresses wish, request or doubt (eu queria que, ela pediu que), and in hypotheses after se. Do not use the indicative imperfect there: say eu queria que ele viesse, not que ele vinha.

examples.en: I wanted you to come earlier.

examples.en: She hoped we knew the answer.

lessons.title: Se + imperfeito do subjuntivo with the futuro do pretérito
lessons.explanation: For a hypothesis that is unreal or unlikely now, put the condition in the imperfect subjunctive after se and the result in the futuro do pretérito: se eu ganhasse na loteria, compraria uma casa. The subjunctive verb is the condition; the conditional verb is the result. In speech, the imperfect indicative often replaces the conditional in the result (eu comprava uma casa), but written Portuguese and this course use the conditional. Do not put the conditional after se: say se eu tivesse tempo, not se eu teria tempo. The two clauses can swap places: eu viajaria mais se tivesse tempo.

lessons.title: Past hypotheses: se tivesse + participle, teria + participle
lessons.explanation: For what would have happened but did not, use the mais-que-perfeito do subjuntivo after se (tivesse + participle) and the futuro do pretérito composto in the result (teria + participle): se eu tivesse estudado, teria passado. The auxiliary is ter, in the imperfect subjunctive in the condition and in the conditional in the result. The participle does not change with the subject: se elas tivessem chegado, teríamos saído. In speech the result often uses the mais-que-perfeito composto (tinha passado). Do not use the future subjunctive here: say se eu tivesse ido, not se eu for ido.

lessons.title: Pretérito perfeito composto do subjuntivo: tenha + participle
lessons.explanation: The perfect subjunctive is tenha, tenhas, tenha, tenhamos, tenham + participle. It places a completed event in the past after a main verb in the present that expresses doubt, emotion or opinion: duvido que ele tenha chegado, fico feliz que vocês tenham vindo, é possível que ela tenha esquecido. It contrasts with the imperfect subjunctive, which follows a past main verb (eu duvidava que ele chegasse). It also appears after talvez and espero que when the event is already finished. Do not use the perfeito indicative after these verbs: say duvido que ele tenha chegado, not duvido que ele chegou.

lessons.title: Indicative or subjunctive: opinion, certainty and doubt
lessons.explanation: After verbs and expressions of certainty and fact use the indicative: acho que, tenho certeza de que, é verdade que, sei que. After doubt, denial and negated opinion use the subjunctive: duvido que, não acho que, não é verdade que, nego que. The same verb can switch mood with the meaning: acho que ele vem (indicative, I believe it) but não acho que ele venha (subjunctive, I doubt it). Talvez, possivelmente and quem sabe also take the subjunctive. The question form do you think that follows the same rule: você acha que ele vem? is neutral, while você não acha que ele venha? expects doubt.
